Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

fail verb

not succeed

also failure, be unsuccessful, it didn’t work, fail an exam, come to nothing, fall through

classical

Ter. And. 670: Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.
Cic. Or. 98 (Lewis & Short): sī quandō minus succēdet

nōn succēdere

verb phrase, intransitive; often impersonal (nōn successit, it didn’t work)

fail, not work out

Of a plan or an attempt: nōn successit, it didn’t work; minus succēdit, it isn’t going well (Lewis & Short s.v. succēdō).

Examples

  • Dēceptus sum, at nōn dēfatīgātus. … Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    I’ve been foiled, but I’m not worn out… That way didn’t work; we’ll go at it another way.Ter. And. 669–670

  • gestit enim nummum in loculōs dēmittere, post hoc sēcūrus cadat an rēctō stet fābula tālō

    For he is eager to drop the money into his purse; after that he does not care whether his play falls flat or stands firm on its feet.Hor. Epist. 2.1.175–176

  • quae cum lagōnae collum frūstrā lamberet, peregrīnam sīc locūtam volucrem accēpimus: sua quisque exempla dēbet aequō animō patī

    As the fox licked the neck of the jar in vain, the stranger bird, so we are told, said: “Everyone should bear patiently being treated as he treats others.”Phaedr. 1.26.10–12

Other words

  • cadō, cadere, cecidī, cāsum — fail, fall flat (of a play); fail (an exam)

    verb, third conjugation, intransitive · also used · classical · Hor. Epist. 2.1.176: sēcūrus cadat an rēctō stet fābula tālō; Traupman 312: in exāmine cadere

    Of a play that fails on the stage, the opposite of stāre (Lewis & Short); hence Traupman’s “fail an exam”. Morgan–Owens (s.v. fail) suggests, with a query, the passive improbārī, to be failed.

  • frūstrā — in vain, without success

    adverb · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.26.10: quae cum lagōnae collum frūstrā lamberet

    With a verb of trying it says that the attempt failed: frūstrā cōnātus est. As a cry, “missed!” (see miss).

  • nihil prōficere — get nowhere, achieve nothing

    also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.20 (Lewis & Short): sī nihil in oppugnātiōne oppidī prōfēcisset

  • ad irritum cadere — come to nothing

    also used · classical · Liv. 2.6 (Lewis & Short): spēs ad irritum cadēns

  • repulsam ferre — be turned down (for a post, in an election)

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.280 (Lewis & Short)

    See apply, for a post.

See also fail, miss, try, apply.
